clue_text: In 1961 this state council heard the word 'Westoxification' for the first time, in the middle of a discussion about reforming Iran's schools.
canonical_answer: Council of the Goals of Education in Iran
accepted_aliases: Council of the Goals of Education in Iran
the Council of the Goals of Education in Iran
شورای اهداف آموزش و پرورش ایران
options: Council of the Goals of Education in Iran
Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution

distractor_rationales.option: Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution
distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A state council that did sit over Iranian schools and universities.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It was created after the 1979 revolution, nineteen years after these meetings.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: A clerical-revolutionary body whose intellectuals also argued about Western influence.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: It was formed in 1979, eighteen years after the 1961 meetings.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The Pahlavi-era council that really did preside over culture and schooling.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The book places the first airing of Westoxification at the meetings of the Council of the Goals of Education in Iran.

explanation: Mirsepassi records that Fardid, as far as we know, introduced the notion of Gharbzadegi ('Westoxification') for the first time at the meetings of the Council of the Goals of Education in Iran in 1961, into a discussion of reforming the Iranian educational system.
book_title: Transnationalism in Iranian Political Thought: The Life and Times of Ahmad Fardid
author: Ali Mirsepassi
supporting_passage: As far as we know, he introduced during these meetings - for the first time - the notion of Gharbzadegi ("Westoxification") into the discussion of reforming the Iranian educational system.

host_reactions.correct_generic: Council of the Goals of Education in Iran. Fardid's word outlived the council that first heard it, which is more than most committees manage.
host_reactions.wrong_generic: Wrong. The word was Westoxification, the year was 1961, and you still reached for a council that did not exist yet.

clue_text: As the nation was pictured as a woman violated by foreign powers, this figure became a powerful symbol of national and masculine humiliation and shame.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Unveiling was the reform the clergy read as surrender to Europe, and she was denounced for it.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: Cronin's chapter works the margins of the modern city, and it hands this symbolic role to the prostitute instead.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: The opium trade ran through foreign hands and its addicts were a standing national scandal.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The addict stood for consumption and decay, not for the nation's sexual dishonour.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Bankruptcy and foreign debt were the era's standard images of national ruin.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The chapter's emblem of a violated nation is a woman's body, and the figure it names is the prostitute.

explanation: Cronin argues that where the nation was figured as a woman violated by foreign powers, the prostitute became a powerful symbol of national and masculine humiliation and shame.
book_title: Social Histories of Iran: Modernism and Marginality in the Middle East
author: Stephanie Cronin
supporting_passage: the prostitute became a powerful symbol of national and masculine humiliation and shame.

host_reactions.correct_generic: The prostitute. The nation's shame needed a body and a price, and it found both on the same street.
host_reactions.wrong_generic: Wrong. You have given the nation's shame a body, just not the one it used.

clue_text: Nima Yushij carries the poetry half of this pairing, and this writer carries the prose half; together the two are named as the pioneers of a modern literary style.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: His 'Once Upon a Time' is routinely called the first real modern Persian short story.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He is the other claimant to that title, but the pairing here is Hedayat in prose with Nima Yushij in poetry.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: His hard, cold fiction is a landmark of twentieth-century Persian prose.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: He comes a generation later; the pioneer named in this pairing is Hedayat.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: He is the most famous modern Persian poet after Nima, and poetry is half of this pairing.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The verse half is already given as Nima Yushij, so the prose half must be Hedayat.

explanation: Gheissari names Sadeq Hedayat (1903-1951) the pioneer of modern Persian prose, pairing him with the poet Nima Yushij (1896-1959) as the two founders of a modern literary style.
book_title: Iranian Intellectuals in the Twentieth Century
author: Ali Gheissari
supporting_passage: pioneers in modern literary style like Sâdeq Hedâyat (1903 –1951), in prose, and Nimâ Yushij (1896 –1959), in poetry

host_reactions.correct_generic: Sadegh Hedayat. He took Persian prose apart on purpose; Nima did the same to the verse, and both are still being blamed for it.
host_reactions.wrong_generic: Wrong. The prose half of that pair is Hedayat, not a poet who arrived a decade later.

clue_text: Told by the authorities to shoot this 1987 film in Pakistan, Mohsen Makhmalbaf went home and filmed 90 percent of it in Iran instead.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It is another early Makhmalbaf feature, and it ran into the censors too.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The film the authorities tried to send abroad was The Cyclist.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: Its whole plot is Makhmalbaf returning to his own 1975 stabbing of a policeman.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: That film dates from 1996 and carried no such condition.

distractor_rationales.why_plausible: It is Makhmalbaf's film about the cinema itself, set outside Tehran.
distractor_rationales.why_wrong: The Pakistan condition was attached to the 1987 film, The Cyclist.

explanation: In Dabashi's interview Makhmalbaf recalls that permission was given only to The Cyclist, and that he was told to shoot it in Pakistan; he filmed about 90 percent of it in Iran and about 10 percent there.
book_title: Close Up: Iranian Cinema, Past, Present and Future
author: Hamid Dabashi
chapter: FIVE ONCE UPON A FILMMAKER: CONVERSATION WITH MOHSEN MA
supporting_passage: and even when I had proposed the project, they told me to shoot the film in Pakistan. I ended up filming 90 percent of it in Iran and about 10 percent in Pakistan.

host_reactions.correct_generic: The Cyclist. The state tried to have this one made abroad and settled for a masterpiece made at home instead.
host_reactions.wrong_generic: Wrong. The film they wanted shot in Pakistan is the one Makhmalbaf brought home.
